name: The Erie Remnant
motto: We were here first. We'll be here last.
description:
The Erie Remnant is a refugee defense militia of about 130 members operating in Cleveland's lakefront districts, formed when the second wave of climate refugees arrived in the late 2170s and found that nobody — not the corporate administration, not Axiom Security, not any existing institution — was going to protect them from the gangs, predators, and exploitation that awaited them in the GLMZ. The Remnant organized out of a refugee camp on the shore of Lake Erie, armed themselves with whatever they could find, and declared their intention to defend the refugee community by any means necessary.

The militia is organized along military lines — not because its founders were military, but because a refugee named Adaeze Okonkwo had read enough history to know that militias without structure become mobs. Okonkwo established a command structure, rules of engagement, and a code of conduct that emphasizes proportional response and civilian protection. The Remnant patrols refugee neighborhoods, escorts work crews to and from employment sites, runs a warning network that alerts the community to incoming threats, and maintains a rapid-response force that can deploy twenty armed fighters within minutes.

The Remnant's members come from everywhere — climate refugees from the Gulf Coast, the Southwest, Southeast Asia, Central America, and the drowned Pacific Islands. This diversity is both strength and vulnerability. The mix of languages, cultures, and backgrounds creates a broad skill set and a resistance to infiltration (it's hard to send a spy into a community where everyone knows everyone), but also generates internal tensions that Okonkwo spends considerable energy managing.

The militia's relationship with other factions is cautious. They'll work with anyone who isn't actively preying on refugees, but they trust no one. The Iron Lotus has made overtures — offering protection in exchange for integration — and the Remnant has declined, recognizing that the Lotus's protection comes with strings that would reduce the refugee community to another revenue source.
ideology: Community defense without compromise. The Erie Remnant believes that refugee communities will always be targets unless they can defend themselves, and that depending on others for protection means accepting their terms. Self-sufficiency in security is not optional — it's the precondition for everything else.
territory: Cleveland's lakefront refugee districts, approximately fifteen blocks of dense residential housing along the Lake Erie shore.
methods: Armed patrol — regular patrols of refugee neighborhoods with visible, uniformed presence
Escort services — armed escorts for work crews, supply runs, and community members traveling outside safe territory
Early warning network — a communication system that alerts the community to approaching threats
Rapid response — a standing force of twenty fighters deployable within minutes to any point in their territory
Community intelligence — leveraging the refugee community's internal communication networks for threat awareness
Diplomatic engagement — cautious relationships with neighboring factions to reduce conflict
resources: 130 members including forty active fighters and ninety support personnel
A military-style command structure with established rules of engagement
An early warning and communication network covering their entire territory
Small arms and improvised weapons — nothing heavy but sufficient for neighborhood defense
A diverse membership with skills drawn from dozens of cultures and professional backgrounds
Community loyalty — the refugee population actively supports and shelters the militia
story_hooks: A corporation wants the lakefront district for development and is funding gangs to make the area unlivable — the Remnant needs proof
Okonkwo has been injured and the succession is unclear — internal factions are forming along cultural lines
A new wave of refugees is arriving and the Remnant doesn't have the resources to absorb them — hard choices about who gets protection
The Remnant captured a gang member who turns out to be a corporate intelligence asset — returning them creates an enemy, keeping them creates a hostage situation
A Remnant patrol crossed into another faction's territory during a pursuit and the diplomatic fallout threatens their network of cautious alliances
